subtopic: Definite Integral as a Limit of a Sum
stem: Evaluate as a limit of sum : \(\int\limits_{1}^{2} (2x + 5)\ dx\)
solution:
Given, \(\int\limits_{1}^{2} (2x + 5)\ dx = \int\limits_{a}^{b} f(x)\ dx\)
\(f(x) = 2x + 5\), \(a = 1\) ; \(b = 2\)
\(\Rightarrow f(a + rh) = f(1 + rh)\)
\(= 2(1 + rh) + 5\)
\(= 2 + 2rh + 5\)
\(= 7 + 2rh\)
and \(h = \dfrac{b - a}{n}\), \(h = \dfrac{2 - 1}{n}\), \(\therefore nh = 1\)
We know \(\int\limits_{a}^{b} f(x)\ dx = \lim\limits_{n \to \infty} \sum\limits_{r = 1}^{n} h \cdot f(a + rh)\)
\(\therefore \int\limits_{1}^{2} (2x + 5)\ dx = \lim\limits_{n \to \infty} \sum\limits_{r = 1}^{n} h \cdot (7 + 2rh)\)
\(= \lim\limits_{n \to \infty} \sum\limits_{r = 1}^{n} (7h + 2rh^{2})\)
\(= \lim\limits_{n \to \infty} \left( 7h \sum\limits_{r = 1}^{n} 1 + 2h^{2} \sum\limits_{r = 1}^{n} r \right)\)
\(= \lim\limits_{n \to \infty} \left[ 7h \cdot (n) + 2h^{2} \left( \dfrac{n(n + 1)}{2} \right) \right]\)
\(= \lim\limits_{n \to \infty} \left[ 7nh + h^{2} n^{2} \left( 1 + \dfrac{1}{n} \right) \right]\)
\(= \lim\limits_{n \to \infty} \left[ 7(1) + (1)^{2} \left( 1 + \dfrac{1}{n} \right) \right]\)
\(= 7 + 1(1 + 0) = 8\)

subtopic: Definite Integral as a Limit of a Sum
stem: Evaluate as a limit of sum : \(\int\limits_{2}^{3} 7^{x}\ dx\)
solution:
[Textbook misprint: although \(a=2\), the book prints \(f(a+rh)=f(1+rh)\), and the line beginning \(\therefore\) prints the integral as \(\int_{1}^{3}7^{x}\,dx\) instead of \(\int_{2}^{3}7^{x}\,dx\). Both are copying slips from the previous example: the working itself uses \(7^{2+rh}\) throughout, so the printed answer \(\dfrac{294}{\log 7}\) is correct. Rewritten here with \(f(2+rh)\) and lower limit 2.]

Given, \(\int\limits_{2}^{3} 7^{x}\ dx = \int\limits_{a}^{b} f(x)\ dx\)
\(f(x) = 7^{x}\), \(a = 2\) ; \(b = 3\)
\(\Rightarrow f(a + rh) = f(1 + rh)\)
\(= 7^{2 + rh}\)
\(= 7^{2} \cdot 7^{rh}\)
and \(h = \dfrac{b - a}{n}\), \(h = \dfrac{3 - 2}{n}\), \(\therefore nh = 1\)
We know \(\int\limits_{a}^{b} f(x)\ dx = \lim\limits_{n \to \infty} \sum\limits_{r = 1}^{n} h \cdot f(a + rh)\)
\(\therefore \int\limits_{1}^{3} 7^{x}\ dx = \lim\limits_{n \to \infty} \sum\limits_{r = 1}^{n} h \cdot \left( 7^{2} \cdot 7^{r \cdot h} \right)\)
\(= \lim\limits_{n \to \infty} 7^{2} \cdot \sum\limits_{r = 1}^{n} h \cdot 7^{r \cdot h}\)
\(= \lim\limits_{n \to \infty} 7^{2} \cdot h \cdot \left[ 7^{h} + 7^{2h} + 7^{3h} + 7^{4h} + \ldots + 7^{nh} \right]\)
\(= \lim\limits_{n \to \infty} 7^{2} \cdot h \cdot \left( \dfrac{7^{h} \left[ (7^{h})^{n} - 1 \right]}{7^{h} - 1} \right) = \lim\limits_{n \to \infty} 7^{2} \cdot \left( \dfrac{7^{h} (7^{nh} - 1)}{\dfrac{7^{h} - 1}{h}} \right)\)
\(= \lim\limits_{n \to \infty} 7^{2} \cdot \left( \dfrac{7^{h} (7^{(1)} - 1)}{\dfrac{7^{h} - 1}{h}} \right)\)
\(= \dfrac{7^{2} \cdot 7^{0} \cdot (7 - 1)}{\log 7} = \dfrac{(49)(1)(6)}{\log 7} = \dfrac{294}{\log 7}\)

subtopic: Definite Integral as a Limit of a Sum
stem: Evaluate as a limit of sum : \(\int\limits_{0}^{4} (x - x^{2})\ dx\)
solution:
\(\int\limits_{0}^{4} (x - x^{2})\ dx = \int\limits_{a}^{b} f(x)\ dx\)
\(f(x) = x - x^{2}\), \(a = 0\) ; \(b = 4\)
\(\Rightarrow f(a + rh) = f(0 + rh)\)
\(= f(rh)\)
\(= (rh) - (rh)^{2}\)
\(= rh - r^{2} h^{2}\)
and \(h = \dfrac{b - a}{n}\), \(h = \dfrac{4 - 0}{n}\), \(\therefore nh = 4\)
We know \(\int\limits_{a}^{b} f(x)\ dx = \lim\limits_{n \to \infty} \sum\limits_{r = 1}^{n} h \cdot [\,f(a + rh)\,]\)
\(\therefore \int\limits_{0}^{4} (x - x^{2})\ dx = \lim\limits_{n \to \infty} \sum\limits_{r = 1}^{n} h \cdot \left( rh - r^{2} h^{2} \right)\)
\(= \lim\limits_{n \to \infty} \sum\limits_{r = 1}^{n} \left( rh^{2} - r^{2} h^{3} \right)\)
\(= \lim\limits_{n \to \infty} \left( h^{2} \cdot \sum\limits_{r = 1}^{n} r - h^{3} \cdot \sum\limits_{r = 1}^{n} r^{2} \right)\)
\(= \lim\limits_{n \to \infty} \left[ h^{2} \left( \dfrac{n(n + 1)}{2} \right) - h^{3} \left( \dfrac{n(n + 1)(2n + 1)}{6} \right) \right]\)
\(= \lim\limits_{n \to \infty} \left[ \dfrac{h^{2} \cdot n \cdot n \left( 1 + \dfrac{1}{n} \right)}{2} - \dfrac{h^{3} \cdot n \cdot n \left( 1 + \dfrac{1}{n} \right) n \left( 2 + \dfrac{1}{n} \right)}{6} \right]\)
\(= \lim\limits_{n \to \infty} \left[ \dfrac{(nh)^{2} \left( 1 + \dfrac{1}{n} \right)}{2} - \dfrac{(nh)^{3} \left( 1 + \dfrac{1}{n} \right) \left( 2 + \dfrac{1}{n} \right)}{6} \right]\)
\(= \lim\limits_{n \to \infty} \left[ \dfrac{(4)^{2} \left( 1 + \dfrac{1}{n} \right)}{2} - \dfrac{(4)^{3} \left( 1 + \dfrac{1}{n} \right) \left( 2 + \dfrac{1}{n} \right)}{6} \right]\)
\(= \dfrac{(4)^{2} \cdot (1 + 0)}{2} - \dfrac{(4)^{3} (1 + 0)(2 + 0)}{6}\)
\(= 8 - \dfrac{(64)(2)}{6}\)
\(= -\dfrac{40}{3}\)

subtopic: Definite Integral as a Limit of a Sum
stem: Evaluate as a limit of sum : \(\int\limits_{0}^{\pi/2} \sin x\ dx\)
solution:
[Textbook misprint: (1) \(\sum\sin rh\) is set equal to a line whose terms have already been multiplied by \(2\sin\dfrac{h}{2}\); (2) in the telescoping tail the \(h\) is printed outside the cosine, \(\cos\left(\dfrac{2n-1}{2}\right)h\), with an unmatched bracket; (3) the book prints \(nh=\dfrac{\pi}{4}\) where it is \(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\); (4) the last-but-one display drops a factor 2, giving denominator \(\dfrac{1}{2}\) instead of 1. The answer 1 is correct.]

\(\int\limits_{0}^{\pi/2} \sin x\ dx = \int\limits_{0}^{\pi/2} f(x)\ dx\)
\(f(x) = \sin x\), \(a = 0\) ; \(b = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\)
\(\Rightarrow f(a + rh) = \sin (a + rh)\)
\(= \sin (0 + rh)\)
\(= \sin rh\)
and \(h = \dfrac{b - a}{n} = \dfrac{\dfrac{\pi}{2} - 0}{n}\), \(\therefore nh = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\)
We know \(\int\limits_{a}^{b} f(x)\ dx = \lim\limits_{n \to \infty} \sum\limits_{r = 1}^{n} h \cdot [\,f(a + rh)\,]\)
\(\therefore \int\limits_{0}^{\pi/2} \sin x\ dx = \lim\limits_{n \to \infty} \sum\limits_{r = 1}^{n} h \cdot \sin rh\)
\(= \lim\limits_{n \to \infty} h \cdot \sum\limits_{r = 1}^{n} \sin rh\)
\(= \lim\limits_{n \to \infty} h \cdot \left[ \sin h + \sin 2h + \sin 3h + \ldots + \sin nh \right]\) . . . (I)
Consider,
\(\sum\limits_{r = 1}^{n} \sin rh = \sin h + \sin 2h + \sin 3h + \ldots + \sin nh\)
\(= 2 \sin \dfrac{h}{2} \cdot \sin h + 2 \sin \dfrac{h}{2} \cdot \sin 2h + 2 \sin \dfrac{h}{2} \cdot \sin 3h + \ldots + 2 \sin \dfrac{h}{2} \cdot \sin nh\)
\(\because 2 \sin \mathrm{A} \cdot \sin \mathrm{B} = \cos (\mathrm{A} - \mathrm{B}) - \cos (\mathrm{A} + \mathrm{B})\)
\(2 \sin \dfrac{h}{2} \cdot \sum\limits_{r = 1}^{n} \sin rh = \left[ \left( \cos \dfrac{h}{2} - \cos \dfrac{3h}{2} \right) + \left( \cos \dfrac{3h}{2} - \cos \dfrac{5h}{2} \right) + \left( \cos \dfrac{5h}{2} - \cos \dfrac{7h}{2} \right) + \ldots \right.\)
\(\left. + \ldots + \left( \cos \left( \dfrac{2n - 1}{2} \right) h - ( \cos \left( \dfrac{2n + 1}{2} \right) h \right] \right.\)
\(= \left[ \cos \dfrac{h}{2} - \cos \left( \dfrac{2n + 1}{2} \right) h \right]\)
\(= \left[ \cos \dfrac{h}{2} - \cos \left( \dfrac{2nh}{2} + \dfrac{h}{2} \right) \right]\)
\(= \left[ \cos \dfrac{h}{2} - \cos \left( \dfrac{\pi}{2} + \dfrac{h}{2} \right) \right]\) \(\because nh = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\)
\(= \left( \cos \dfrac{h}{2} + \sin \dfrac{h}{2} \right)\)
\(\therefore \sum\limits_{r = 1}^{n} \sin rh = \dfrac{\cos \dfrac{h}{2} + \sin \dfrac{h}{2}}{2 \sin \dfrac{h}{2}}\)
Now from I,
\(\int\limits_{0}^{\pi/2} \sin x \cdot dx = \lim\limits_{n \to \infty} \sum\limits_{r = 1}^{n} h \cdot \sin rh\)
\(= \lim\limits_{n \to \infty} h \cdot \left[ \dfrac{\cos \dfrac{h}{2} + \sin \dfrac{h}{2}}{2 \sin \dfrac{h}{2}} \right]\)
\(\because nh = \dfrac{\pi}{4}\) as \(n \to \infty \Rightarrow h \to 0\) \(\left( \dfrac{1}{n} \to 0 \right)\)
\(= \lim\limits_{\substack{n \to \infty \\ h \to 0}} \left[ \dfrac{\cos \dfrac{h}{2} + \sin \dfrac{h}{2}}{\dfrac{2 \cdot \sin \dfrac{h}{2}}{h}} \right]\)
\(= \dfrac{\cos 0 + \sin 0}{\left( \dfrac{1}{2} \right)}\)
\(= \dfrac{1 + 0}{2 \cdot \dfrac{1}{2}} = 1\)
\(\therefore \int\limits_{0}^{\pi/2} \sin x\ dx = 1\)
